findings.evidence: In `pkg/planner/cardinality/row_count_index.go:456` the index-stats fallback calls `GetRowCountByIndexRanges`; on success it `break`s at `pkg/planner/cardinality/row_count_index.go:457` before `selectivity` is assigned (only assigned in the error path at `pkg/planner/cardinality/row_count_index.go:460-461`), then appends the still-zero `selectivity` at `pkg/planner/cardinality/row_count_index.go:470`. First-parent behavior appended `count` then converted to selectivity later (`bf166d9^1:pkg/planner/cardinality/row_count_index.go:452` and `bf166d9^1:pkg/planner/cardinality/row_count_index.go:469-472`), so this regression is introduced here. Checked later history: the same pattern still exists on `upstream-master` (`pkg/planner/cardinality/row_count_index.go:485-487` breaks before setting `selectivity`, which is only set at `pkg/planner/cardinality/row_count_index.go:489-490`).
findings.fix: In `expBackoffEstimation`, compute `realtimeCnt` and assign `selectivity = count/float64(realtimeCnt)` (or using the returned count struct) on the success path before breaking. Minimal change: move the `realtimeCnt`+`selectivity` assignment to immediately after the `GetRowCountByIndexRanges` call and before `if err == nil { break }`, or store the last successful `count`/`idxStats` and compute `selectivity` after the loop. Consider clamping selectivity to `[0,1]` and guarding `realtimeCnt==0` to avoid `0/0` NaNs.
findings.impact: When a column’s stats are missing/invalid and `expBackoffEstimation` falls back to other index stats (`coll.ColID2IdxIDs`), successful lookups will append a zero selectivity. This can drive exponential-backoff selectivity to 0, making interval range row-count estimates collapse to 0 and skipping the normal histogram fallback, leading to extreme underestimation and potentially severe plan/cost selection regressions.
findings.later_fix_evidence: No fix found up to `upstream-master`; the same break-before-assign pattern still appears in `pkg/planner/cardinality/row_count_index.go:485-490` on `upstream-master`.
findings.verify: Add a targeted unit test (planner/cardinality) that forces `expBackoffEstimation` to take the index-stats fallback: construct a multi-column range where a referenced column’s `coll.Columns[colID]` is invalid/missing but `coll.ColID2IdxIDs[colID]` contains a valid alternative index; assert `expBackoffEstimation` returns `success=true` and `sel>0` (and that `getIndexRowCountForStatsV2` doesn’t return 0 for a clearly non-empty range). Regression-check with the existing planner/cardinality tests around out-of-range and exponential backoff logic.
findings.what: `expBackoffEstimation` regression: index-stats fallback can leave `selectivity` unset (0) on successful `GetRowCountByIndexRanges`, causing exponential-backoff selectivity/rowcount to collapse to 0.
